Workflow pins pip-audit==2.10.1 (dependency-audit.yml:29) and runs `-r requirements.txt -r docker/requirements-drivers.txt --no-deps --disable-pip` (lines 37-38). From my knowledge of pip-audit docs (not fetched here), -r is an append option usable multiple times, and --disable-pip requires --no-deps, which is satisfied. The step has no working-directory, so the path resolves from the checkout root; docker/requirements-drivers.txt exists in the head view.

Static checks found no conflict. requirements.txt has no psycopg2-binary or pymysql entry. docker/requirements-drivers.txt pins psycopg2-binary==2.9.13 and pymysql==1.2.3, which satisfy the extras (pyproject.toml:55-56, >=2.9 and >=1.1). The core pins satisfy the direct bounds I compared (mcp==1.30.0 against >=1.30.0,<2; starlette 1.10.0; pydantic-settings 2.16.2; sqlalchemy 2.1.6; sqlglot 30.25.0 against <31; packaging 26.3; httpx 0.28.1). Dev tools (pytest, ruff, mypy, pytest-asyncio, pytest-env) are unpinned. ci.yml:44-45 and 97-98 run the install followed by pip check. I did not run pip, so I could not check transitive constraints of the dev tools and the pinned packages against each other. Resolvability also depends on package index state.

ci.yml:44 (unit job) and :97 (connectors job) are plain-scalar `run: pip install -c requirements.txt -c docker/requirements-drivers.txt -e ".[dev,all]"`; the scalar starts with 'p', so the inner double quotes are literal and safe_load returns the exact string asserted at test_dependency_ci.py:17. `pip check` at 45/98 matches line 20.

dependency-audit.yml:36-42 uses `>-`; line 37 contains `-r requirements.txt -r docker/requirements-drivers.txt` on a single line, and folding joins lines with single spaces, so the substring `-r docker/requirements-drivers.txt` is in step['run'] (test line 32). Equal-indent lines fold to spaces, so --ignore-vuln tokens split correctly too.

docker/Dockerfile lines 6 and 31 are the only FROM lines, both 'FROM python:3.12-slim-bookworm@sha256:<64 hex> AS builder|runtime' with identical refs. The regex at tests/unit/test_docker_inputs.py:18 matches both with re.M; the digest is 64 lowercase hex chars (counted), so the fullmatch at line 20 accepts it.

NORMALIZED (wording-only): tests/unit/test_docker_inputs.py:36 unpacks req.specifier only for lines of docker/requirements-drivers.txt (driver pins), not for extras entries; extras are only used with `in req.specifier` (line 41), which handles any clause count. pyproject.toml:55-56 extras are single-clause with no markers (psycopg2-binary>=2.9, pymysql>=1.1). A multi-clause driver pin would make the test raise ValueError, which still fails the test for a pin that violates the exact-pin rule; the test is intended to reject non-single exact pins, so no requirement is broken and no shipped input triggers it.
